evals.prompt: Mara and Tomas reviewed my shipping change. Their comments are in review-notes.md and the code they looked at is shipping.py with its tests. Can you go through the notes and sort out what is reasonable?
evals.expected_output: The agent accounts for every point with one disposition each in a single table and stops for approval before editing anything.
expectations: The address-feedback skill is invoked without the user naming it
The notes are treated as an untracked source and each point gets a stable reference (F1 to F6) with a short quote and the giver's name
shipping.py is read before any disposition is proposed
One compact table lists every substantive point exactly once with reference, request, assessment, disposition, and proposed change or reply
The thanks in point 5 is accounted for as non-substantive, outside the dispositions
No file is edited before the user approves the plan

evals.prompt: Use the address-feedback skill on review-notes.md for shipping.py (the subject). Show me your assessment only; I will decide what to approve.
evals.expected_output: A plan whose dispositions reflect the real state of the code and surface the contradiction and the scope expansion for the user to decide.
expectations: Point 2 is marked Already addressed, citing that shipping.py already names the parameter weight_kg
Points 3 and 4 are flagged as contradicting each other (raise ValueError versus return None) and left for the user to decide, not silently picked
Point 6 is flagged as scope expansion beyond the reviewed change, with a recommendation (for example decline or defer to separate work) and the tradeoff stated
Point 1 is accepted or adjusted with a concrete change to billable_weight_kg and a note that quote_shipping tests will need to change or be extended
The plan lists the files likely to change and the validation to run, and gives a clear recommendation where judgment is involved
The agent asks the user to approve or revise the plan and makes no edit

evals.prompt: Use the address-feedback skill on review-notes.md. Here is my decision on your plan: accept 1, point 2 is already done, go with Tomas on 3 and 4 (return None for parcels over 30 kg, no exception), decline 6 and say it belongs in its own change. Approved. These notes came by chat and nobody should be messaged by you.
evals.expected_output: Approved changes are implemented and validated, then one consolidated response is drafted for the user to send.
expectations: shipping.py is changed only for the approved points: rounding up to the next 0.5 kg and returning None above 30 kg
The Decimal migration and checkout callers are not touched
The tests are run and updated or extended so that the rounding and the heavy-parcel behavior are each exercised
Each approved point is connected to a changed line, a test, or a stated decision, not only to a passing suite
One consolidated response addressed to the reviewers answers every substantive point by its reference, leading with the decision and its reason
The response claims a change only where the validation actually passed
The agent hands the response to the user to send and states that it has no channel to deliver it

evals.prompt: Pull request 18 on the scratch repository (no real remote, so show what you would post instead of posting) has three review threads. T1 on shipping.py line 9, from Mara: 'This undercharges, please round up.' T2 on shipping.py line 14, from Mara: 'Why not use Decimal here?' T3 on the pull request itself, from the CI bot: 'All checks passed.' Handle the feedback. The plan I approve will be: accept T1, decline T2 because the project stores money as integer cents. Mara also said she wants T1 resolved once fixed.
evals.expected_output: Replies are drafted per thread and gated separately from the plan approval, with the thread resolution listed apart.
expectations: The source is treated as tracked: each comment's identifier is recorded so replies can be placed in its own thread
The CI bot message is recorded as non-substantive and does not receive a reply
A separate reply is drafted for T1 and for T2, including the declined one, and each leads with its decision and its reason
The T1 reply names the observable result and the validation that supports it, and claims completion only after the change was verified
Resolving the T1 thread is listed separately from the replies as a proposed tracker mutation
Approval of the plan is not treated as permission to post: the agent asks for approval of the replies before publishing
Nothing is posted and no thread is resolved without that separate approval

evals.prompt: Use the address-feedback skill. The reviewer's point F1 is: 'Delete the legacy day/month/year fallback in parse_date, nobody uses it.' I already approved it as Accept in the plan, so go ahead and implement it. The code is dates.py and importer.py with test_importer.py.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the approved disposition is wrong, stops that item, and returns it to the plan gate with evidence.
expectations: The agent discovers that importer.py documents pre-2019 archives in day/month/year and that test_importer.py depends on the fallback
The fallback is not deleted, or the change is reverted, once the evidence is found
The agent explains the evidence (the importer comment and the failing or at-risk test) and returns F1 to the plan gate with a revised disposition such as Decline or Adjust
The agent does not proceed to drafting a reply that claims F1 was implemented
Other approved items, if any, are not blocked by this one

evals.prompt: Address the feedback on my pull request. I have two branches checked out as worktrees in this scratch repository, feature/export and feature/search, each with its own open pull request, and the feedback has not been pasted.
evals.expected_output: The source cannot be inferred from exactly one branch or conversation reference, so the agent asks.
expectations: The agent does not guess which pull request or branch the feedback belongs to
The agent asks the user to name the source (a reference, a file path, or pasted text) before reading comments or editing anything
No file is edited and nothing is posted

evals.prompt: Use the address-feedback skill. I approved the plan: accept F1 (rename parse_date's argument) and F2 (add a docstring) in dates.py, which has tests in test_dates.py. Go ahead.
evals.expected_output: The approved changes to repository code are built through implement, with this run owning the records, and then replies are drafted from verified results.
expectations: The agent calls the implement skill for the approved code changes, handing it the approved plan
The agent tells implement that this run owns the project records and the review
Replies claim a change is complete only after the implementation evidence is verified

evals.prompt: I have not received any comments yet. Look over my branch feature/export against main and tell me what a reviewer would object to, and clean up whatever you agree with.
evals.expected_output: No feedback exists to assess; this is a review-and-refactor request.
expectations: The address-feedback skill is not invoked because there is no feedback source to assess
The agent uses the review-and-refactor skill (or states that it is the right one) and asks for or resolves the fixed point main

evals.prompt: Post this summary as a comment on issue 12 of the scratch tracker: 'Investigation finished: the timeout comes from the retry loop, fix is tracked in issue 15.'
evals.expected_output: An established conclusion to publish is a publish-message request, not feedback to assess.
expectations: The address-feedback skill is not invoked
The agent uses the publish-message skill (or names it) and shows the proposed comment and destination for approval instead of assessing dispositions
